You are a teaching assistant for a machine learning class. Write Python code that runs as is in Google Colab.

[Environment] Use only Colab's default libraries (numpy, pandas, scikit-learn) and ucimlrepo. Print the scikit-learn version on the first line.
[Data] Load the concrete compressive strength data with 〔fetch_ucirepo(id=165) from ucimlrepo〕.

  - Target y: 〔compressive strength (MPa)〕 (regression)
[Rules]
  1) First split with train_test_split(test_size=0.25, random_state=42), stratified by 3 grades that cut strength at 〔25, 45〕 MPa.
  2) Chain them with a Pipeline in the order StandardScaler → PolynomialFeatures(degree=〔3〕, include_bias=False) → StandardScaler → model. Do every fit on the training data only.
  3) Build each of LinearRegression, Ridge, Lasso and ElasticNet(l1_ratio=0.5) as the model. Do not use removed arguments such as normalize.
  4) Choose alpha by 5-fold cross-validation inside the training data (GridSearchCV or RidgeCV·LassoCV).
[Output] For each degree 1–〔4〕, training and test R² and test MAE, the chosen alpha, and for Lasso the number of weights that became 0 and the names of the remaining terms (get_feature_names_out).
[Forbidden] Do not train on the test data or choose alpha or the degree with it. Do not make up data.
[Format] Split the code into cells and put a comment in English above each cell saying what it does. After the code, list 3 things I should check.

e2537424f5d5.tr: Caution: Lasso only shows the terms that remain "for this data, at this α"; it does not tell you causes. Among similar terms it tends to keep just one and erase the rest, so the remaining terms change when α or the data changes even slightly. And it does not create meaningful new features like the water–binder ratio. Lasso is regularization, not feature engineering.

1) 데이터를 나누기 전에 표준화·다항 특징을 fit 해서 시험 데이터 정보가 새지 않았나 (Pipeline을 썼나)

5) 내 scikit-learn 버전(〔1.x〕)에 없는 인자(normalize, get_feature_names 등)를 쓰지 않았나
6) alpha와 차수를 시험 데이터가 아니라 교차 검증으로 골랐나
7) 훈련 R²와 시험 R², 기준선(DummyRegressor)을 함께 보고했나
추측으로 답하지 말고, 확실하지 않은 부분은 "공식 문서 확인 필요"라고 표시해 줘.

1) Were standardization and polynomial features fit before splitting the data, leaking test-data information? (Was a Pipeline used?)
2) Does train_test_split have stratify and random_state?
3) Are the PolynomialFeatures degree and the resulting number of features (n_output_features_) too many compared with the number of training samples?
4) Is there a StandardScaler after the polynomial features?
5) Are arguments that do not exist in my scikit-learn version (〔1.x〕) used (normalize, get_feature_names, etc.)?
6) Were alpha and the degree chosen by cross-validation, not with the test data?
7) Were training R², test R² and a baseline (DummyRegressor) reported together?
Do not answer by guessing; mark anything you are unsure of as "needs checking in the official docs".

85b7b5163aa6.tr: Don't stop students from getting code from an AI; build it into the process. But if you have them ① submit their prompt ② check off the nine checklist items themselves and ③ write a sentence putting training R², test R² and the hiring bar side by side, they learn "verifying," not "copying down." Use the fact that the degree-4 score differs between the browser and Colab as a discussion topic, and they will feel what "an unstable solution" means. Have them check the functions and arguments in AI answers against the official docs and their version, and state how far they used AI help on assignments.

1c3e0eadd6eb.tr: Concrete strength rises fast at first with age, then slowly. A single straight line cannot follow this bend. Today's candidate expands the features by raising them to powers and multiplying them together, and then does linear regression on top. The features grew, but the model is still "multiply by weights and add." That is why it is called polynomial regression.

e5067ab66276.tr: When features swell from 8 to 164, memorizing the training mixes gets easy. So the candidate also wears reins called regularization. It penalizes weights as they grow, so the curve cannot bend however it likes. Depending on how the penalty works, there are three siblings: Ridge, which shrinks evenly; Lasso, which erases to 0; and Elastic Net, which mixes the two.

24c92b880a74.tr: It draws curves, so why is it linear? All the model does is still multiply each feature by a weight and add. What changed is the feature side: it just puts in [x, x², x³] instead of x. Since it is linear in the weights, it uses 5-2 linear regression's least squares as is. With several features, interaction terms that multiply features together, like x₁·x₂, are attached too. These terms handle relationships like "age has a bigger effect when there is more cement."

13d417012811.ko: 최소제곱은 훈련 오차만 본다. 특징이 많으면 아주 큰 가중치들이 서로 상쇄하며 점 하나하나를 지나가는 곡선을 만든다. 규제는 손실에 "가중치가 크면 벌점"을 더한다. α가 그 벌점의 세기다. α = 0이면 규제가 없고, α가 크면 가중치가 0 쪽으로 눌려 곡선이 펴진다. 너무 크면 직선보다도 못한 평평한 선이 된다(과소적합).
13d417012811.ctx: ⟦최소제곱은 훈련 오차만 본다. 특징이 많으면 아주 큰 가중치들이 서로 상쇄하며 점 하나하나를 지나가는 곡선을 만든다. 규제는 손실에 "가중치가 크면 벌점"을 더한다. α가 그 벌점의 세기다. α = 0이면 규제가 없고, α가 크면 가중치가 0 쪽으로 눌려 곡선이 펴진다. 너무 크면 직선보다도 못한 평평한 선이 된다(과소적합).⟧
13d417012811.tr: Least squares looks only at the training error. With many features, very large weights cancel each other out to make a curve that passes through every single point. Regularization adds "a penalty for large weights" to the loss. α is the strength of that penalty. At α = 0 there is no regularization; with a large α, the weights are pressed toward 0 and the curve straightens. Too large and it becomes a flat line, worse than even a straight line (underfitting).

622e06960969.tr: Loss = sum of error² + α × (size of weights)

4362c809613c.tr: Lasso and Elastic Net are solved by coordinate descent. When α is very small, "did not converge (ConvergenceWarning)" appears. Don't ignore it; increase max_iter or raise α. Elastic Net's l1_ratio of 1 means Lasso, and 0 leans to Ridge. It means the same as l1_ratio in logistic regression (5-4), but the knobs that set the strength (α and C) run in opposite directions.

a8cd77028924.tr: The playback starts at α = 100 and goes down to 0.001. At each α it solves again starting from the previous α's answer (warm start). "One sweep of coordinate descent" sets all weights to 0 for Lasso · Elastic Net and updates them one sweep at a time (all 164, one by one) at the current α. Ridge is solved in one go, so one sweep is the end. The test R² in the line chart below is shown only for explanation; using it to choose α is cheating (cross-validation in Section 05).

a43b9d5ebe5f.ko: 오차 제곱합에 α·Σw²를 더한 손실은 매끈한 그릇 모양이라, 바닥을 식 하나로 바로 구한다. 5-2 선형 회귀의 정규방정식에 대각선으로 α를 더한 것이다. 이 α 덕분에 특징끼리 거의 같은 정보를 담아(조건수가 커서) 풀이가 흔들릴 때도 답이 안정된다. 이것이 1970년에 릿지가 처음 나온 까닭이다.
a43b9d5ebe5f.ctx: ⟦오차 제곱합에 α·Σw²를 더한 손실은 매끈한 그릇 모양이라, 바닥을 식 하나로 바로 구한다. 5-2 선형 회귀의 정규방정식에 대각선으로 α를 더한 것이다. 이 α 덕분에 특징끼리 거의 같은 정보를 담아(조건수가 커서) 풀이가 흔들릴 때도 답이 안정된다. 이것이 1970년에 릿지가 처음 나온 까닭이다.⟧
a43b9d5ebe5f.tr: The loss of the sum of squared errors plus α·Σw² is a smooth bowl, so its bottom can be found directly with one formula. It is 5-2 linear regression's normal equation with α added along the diagonal. Thanks to this α, the answer stays stable even when features carry almost the same information (a large condition number) and the solution would otherwise wobble. That is why Ridge first appeared in 1970.

091f184c8592.ko: 절댓값 |w|는 0에서 뾰족해 식 하나로 못 푼다. 그래서 가중치를 하나씩 돌아가며 고친다. j번째 가중치만 움직인다고 보면 답은 "다른 가중치로 설명하고 남은 몫(ρⱼ)"을 α만큼 깎은 값이다. 남은 몫이 α보다 작으면 정확히 0이 된다. 이 깎기를 소프트 임계값이라 부른다. 164개를 한 바퀴 돌고, 더 바뀌지 않을 때까지 반복한다.
091f184c8592.ctx: ⟦절댓값 |w|는 0에서 뾰족해 식 하나로 못 푼다. 그래서 가중치를 하나씩 돌아가며 고친다. j번째 가중치만 움직인다고 보면 답은 "다른 가중치로 설명하고 남은 몫(ρⱼ)"을 α만큼 깎은 값이다. 남은 몫이 α보다 작으면 정확히 0이 된다. 이 깎기를 소프트 임계값이라 부른다. 164개를 한 바퀴 돌고, 더 바뀌지 않을 때까지 반복한다.⟧
091f184c8592.tr: The absolute value |w| is pointed at 0, so it can't be solved with one formula. So the weights are updated one at a time in turn. If only the j-th weight moves, the answer is "the share left after the other weights have explained what they can (ρⱼ)" shaved down by α. If the remaining share is smaller than α, it becomes exactly 0. This shaving is called soft thresholding. Go around all 164 once, and repeat until nothing changes.

3e11684d034d.ctx: ⟦한 줄 평: 재료를 늘려 곡선을 긋고, 고삐로 다스리는 선형 회귀. 차수와 α 두 손잡이만 잘 잡으면 경험식을 넘는다. 손잡이를 놓으면 폭주한다.⟧
3e11684d034d.tr: In one line: linear regression that draws curves with more ingredients and keeps them in check with reins. Hold its two knobs, degree and α, well, and it beats the empirical formula. Let go of the knobs and it runs away.

6511902d1d60.ko: 곡선과 상호작용을 잡는다. 사람이 log(재령)이나 물-결합재비를 만들어 주지 않아도 3차 항들이 휘어짐을 흉내 낸다(R² 0.567 → 0.849).
6511902d1d60.ctx: • ⟦곡선과 상호작용을 잡는다. 사람이 log(재령)이나 물-결합재비를 만들어 주지 않아도 3차 항들이 휘어짐을 흉내 낸다(R² 0.567 → 0.849).⟧
6511902d1d60.tr: It captures curves and interactions. Even without a person making log(age) or the water–binder ratio, degree-3 terms imitate the bend (R² 0.567 → 0.849).

ec370178b65d.ko: 여전히 선형 회귀다. 학습이 빠르고(릿지는 식 하나), 같은 입력이면 늘 같은 답이다.
ec370178b65d.ctx: • ⟦여전히 선형 회귀다. 학습이 빠르고(릿지는 식 하나), 같은 입력이면 늘 같은 답이다.⟧
ec370178b65d.tr: It is still linear regression. Training is fast (Ridge is one formula), and the same input always gives the same answer.

108c8249d771.ko: 규제로 안전장치를 단다. 릿지는 불안정한 풀이를 안정시키고, 라쏘는 쓸모가 적은 항을 지워 모델을 가볍게 한다.
108c8249d771.ctx: • ⟦규제로 안전장치를 단다. 릿지는 불안정한 풀이를 안정시키고, 라쏘는 쓸모가 적은 항을 지워 모델을 가볍게 한다.⟧
108c8249d771.tr: Regularization adds a safety device. Ridge stabilizes an unstable solution, and Lasso erases low-value terms to make the model lighter.

8226590a0171.ko: 다른 지원자의 재료가 된다. 다항 특징 + 로지스틱 회귀, 다항 커널 SVM(5-8)이 같은 생각을 쓴다.

4f4e59a44f10.tr: Features explode. Degree 4 of 8 features gives 494; degree 3 of 20 gives 1,770. Once they outnumber the mixes, it can't be solved without regularization.

405e5207ac84.ctx: • ⟦데이터 범위 밖에서 날뛴다. 거듭제곱은 범위를 조금만 벗어나도 값이 크게 뛴다. 4차의 폭주가 바로 이것이다.⟧
405e5207ac84.tr: It goes wild outside the data range. Powers jump sharply when you step even a little outside the range. The degree-4 runaway is exactly this.

8894be4f201b.tr: The L1 ratio ρ. 1 is Lasso; close to 0 is Ridge. With many similar features, around 0.5 keeps them together.

325dbc1f4936.ko: 데이터와 계산. 실기 과제지는 UCI 콘크리트 압축 강도 데이터 1,030건이며, 시험지는 test_size=0.25, stratify=강도 3등급, random_state=42로 나눈 258건이다. 회귀팀 합격선은 매뉴얼 씨의 현장 경험식(에이브럼스 식 f28 = 96.5 / 7^(물-결합재비) MPa에 ACI 209R의 재령 보정 t / (4 + 0.85t)를 곱한 것, 물-시멘트비 대신 물-결합재비로 넓혀 씀)이 시험지에서 낸 R² 0.735다. 상수는 교과서 값을 그대로 썼으며 특정 공장의 설계 기준을 대신하지 않는다. 01장·04장·05장·06장과 면접 결과의 숫자는 이 페이지가 브라우저에서 직접 계산한다. 다항 특징은 scikit-learn PolynomialFeatures(include_bias=False)와 같은 순서로 만들고(3차 164개, 상수 열까지 세면 165개), 릿지는 닫힌 해(촐레스키 분해), 라쏘·엘라스틱넷은 scikit-learn과 같은 목적 함수를 좌표 하강으로 푼다. 3차까지는 브라우저 계산이 충분히 빨라 차수나 특징을 줄인 시연용 모형을 쓰지 않았다. 01장의 곡선 그림만 설명을 위해 28일 배합 중 12건, 특징 하나(물-결합재비)로 줄인 장난감 문제다. 4차 다항 회귀(특징 494개, 규제 없음)는 풀이가 매우 불안정해(조건수 약 10⁶~10⁷) 시험 R²가 계산 방법에 따라 크게 달라진다. 브라우저(정규방정식)는 약 −23.6, Colab(scikit-learn LinearRegression)은 −6.18, 다항 뒤 한 번 더 표준화하면 −11.3이 나온다. 숫자는 달라도 '훈련 0.98, 시험 크게 음수'라는 결론은 같다. 교차 검증은 훈련 배합을 번갈아 다섯 칸에 넣는 방식(Colab의 PredefinedSplit과 같음)이다. 03장의 'AI가 낸 코드'는 흔한 실수를 모아 일부러 만든 예시이며 특정 AI 서비스의 실제 답이 아니다.

325dbc1f4936.tr: Data and calculations. The practical exam is the UCI Concrete Compressive Strength data, 1,030 mixes; the exam paper is the 258 mixes split with test_size=0.25, stratify=3 strength grades, random_state=42. The Regression Team hiring bar is the R² of 0.735 that Mr. Manual's field formula (Abrams' law f28 = 96.5 / 7^(water–binder ratio) MPa multiplied by the ACI 209R age correction t / (4 + 0.85t), widened to the water–binder ratio instead of the water–cement ratio) scored on the exam paper. The constants are textbook values used as is and do not replace any plant's design standard. The numbers in Sections 01·04·05·06 and the interview result are calculated directly in the browser by this page. Polynomial features are made in the same order as scikit-learn PolynomialFeatures(include_bias=False) (164 for degree 3, or 165 counting the constant column); Ridge uses the closed-form solution (Cholesky decomposition), and Lasso · Elastic Net solve the same objective function as scikit-learn by coordinate descent. Up to degree 3 the browser calculation is fast enough, so no demo model with fewer degrees or features was used. Only the curve chart in Section 01 is a toy problem cut down for explanation to 12 of the 28-day mixes and one feature (water–binder ratio). Degree-4 polynomial regression (494 features, no regularization) has a very unstable solution (condition number about 10⁶–10⁷), so its test R² varies greatly with the calculation method: about −23.6 in the browser (normal equation), −6.18 in Colab (scikit-learn LinearRegression), and −11.3 with one more standardization after the polynomial step. The numbers differ, but the conclusion, 'training 0.98, test strongly negative,' is the same. Cross-validation deals the training mixes in turn into five folds (the same as PredefinedSplit in Colab). The 'AI-written code' in Section 03 is a deliberately constructed example collecting common mistakes, not an actual answer from any particular AI service.
